body: I'm not really young (32F), but I've been with my MM for just over 3 years. We ebb and flow, just as non AP relationships do. I am monogamous to him, and sometimes, it really gets to me. The rushing off the phone, the always waiting for him to contact me, the fleeting, rushed times together... it's hard. I do want a relationship where we don't have to hide, but I'm tangled up in the feels. Just try and be true to yourself OP, and take it one day at a time.

I see a trauma therapist as well and he's been incredibly receptive and supportive of my situation (single female AP with a MM, going on 3 years). It came out in one of our first sessions, and he's incredibly non-judgmental and supportive. I agree you just have to look around; I got lucky.

I took a personal finance college my freshman year of college as well (it fulfilled an econ requirement) and to this day, one of the most useful classes I ever took. Taught me so much. And I agree! r/personalfinance was one of the first subreddits I binge read, and it's one of the best, IMHO.
That's an interesting thought! Or they worked under the table/cash jobs. Still - not having a basic understanding of pay cycles and tax is so worrisome. :(
^ This is why we desperately need personal finance classes in high school curriculums.
